senses.gloss: (neut. verb) to go away, go aside, depart; to keep off.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 1:5">Yoma I, 5</cite> <he>הוא פוֹרֵשׁ … פּוֹרְשִׁין וכ׳</he> he turned aside and wept, and so did they.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 1:10:4">Y. Keth. I, 25ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>ראו אותו פורש מציפורין</he> they saw him come out of Sepphoris (so that he is presumably an inhabitant of Sepphoris); <he>פירש מן הבתים</he> they saw him leave one of the houses of Sepphoris.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 9:16">Num. R. s. 9</cite> <he>את פָּרַשְׁתְּ מדרך וכ׳</he> thou didst depart from the way (disregard the customs) of Israel’s daughters.

<cite ref="Zevachim 113a:8">Zeb. 113ᵃ</cite> (play on <cite ref="Q02033"><he>פרשה</he></cite>, <cite ref="Numbers 19:5">Num. XIX, 5</cite>) <he>מקים שפּוֹרֶשֶׁת למיתה וכ׳</he> there where she departs for death, she shall be burnt.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 1:2:8">Y. M. Kat. I, 80ᵇ</cite> bot. (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 13:45">Lev. XIII, 45</cite>) <he>כדי שתהא טומאה … פְּרוֹשׁ</he> that the uncleanness itself may cry out …, ‘keep off’; Y. Maas. Sh. V, beg. 55ᵈ; a. fr.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 946">Yalk. Prov. 946</cite>; Yalk. Num. 738 <he>הספינות פּוֹרְשׁוֹת בים</he> the ships make their way through the sea.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 10:1">Num. R. s. 10</cite> <he>כשם שאדם פירש את עצמו וכ׳</he> as a person keeps himself away (abstains) from the fruits of Orlah, so will those who misbehave towards their handmaids, be separated from the virtuous on the day of judgment.; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="Q01738"><he>פָּרוּשׁ</he></cite>, q. v.

senses.gloss: (cmp. פָּרַט) to single out, specify, speak distinctly. Ib. (expl. יַפְלִא, Num. VI, 2) כשיִפְרוֹשׁ לנדור וכ׳ when he speaks out his vow, to the exclusion of him who thinks it in his heart; a. fr.—
units: <cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 24">Sifré Num. 24</cite> <he>עד שיפרוש לך … כדרך שפירש וכ׳</he> (<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 710">Yalk. ib. 710</cite> <he>שיפרוט … שפרט</he>), v. <cite ref="Q01763"><he>פָּרַט</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 22">Lev. R. s. 22</cite> <he>והן נִפְרָשִׁים מעבודה זרה</he> and thus they will be kept away from idolatrous worship; a. e.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 82b:2">Snh. 82ᵇ</cite> <he>היה לו</he> … <he>לפרוש ולא פי׳</he> Zimri might have withdrawn (from the woman), but he did not.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 82a:10">Ib.ᵃ</cite> <he>אם פ׳ וכ׳</he> if Z. had withdrawn, and Phineas had slain him &c.
<cite ref="Pesachim 87b:4">Pes. 87ᵇ</cite> <he>פ׳ מן האשה</he> withdrew from contact with his wife.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 20">Gen. R. s. 20</cite> <he>שפֵּירְשָׁה חיה מאדם</he> that Eve was separated from Adam.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 86b:3">Sabb. 86ᵇ</cite> <he>פירשה מן האיש</he> the semen issued from a man.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 49b:11">Pes. 49ᵇ</cite> <he>שנה ופ׳ קשה וכ׳</he> he that studied and gave it up, is the worst of all (in hostility to scholars); a. fr.

senses.gloss: to go on a voyage; to cross the ocean (cmp. פָּלַג Hif.). Y. M. Kat. III, beg. 81ᶜ אסור לפָרֵשׁ לים הגדול it is forbidden to start on a sea voyage (during the festive week). Y. Yeb. XVI, 15ᵈ top עשיתי מְפָרֵשׁ וכ׳ I was crossing &c. Y. Meg. II, 73ᵇ top מְפָרְשֵׁי ימים voyagers on the sea; a. fr.

units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 22:9">Gen. R. s. 22</cite> <he>אילו רצה המלך פֵּירְשָׁן ולא רצה המלך לפָרְשָׁן</he> if the king desired it, he would separate them (the fighters), but the king does not wish to separate them; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 38:3">Yalk. ib. 38</cite>.

senses.gloss: to specify, express clearly. Ib. א״א לפה לפָרְשוֹ no mouth can express it.
units: <cite ref="Menachot 91a:9">Men. 91ᵃ</cite> <he>דמְפָרֵשׁ</he> when he (in making his vow) specified (‘sheep’ or ‘cattle’), opp. <he>בסתמא</he>.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 6">Gen. R. s. 6</cite> <he>אנשי … פֵּירְשׁוּ אותו</he> the men of the Great Assembly said it plainly.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:5">Snh. VII, 5</cite> <he>עד שיְפָרֵשׁ השם</he> until he mentions the Name expressly (uses the Tetragrammaton), opp. <cite ref="K00566"><he>כִּינּוּי</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Gittin 36a:6">Gitt. 36ᵃ</cite> <he>שיהו עדים מְפָרְשִׁין שמותיהן</he> that witnesses must sign their full names; a. fr.—Part. pass. <he>מְפוֹרָשׁ</he>, f. <he>מְפוֹרֶשֶׁת</he>; pl. <he>מְפוֹרָשִׁים</he>, <he>מְפוֹרָשִׁין</he>; <he>מְפוֹרָשׁוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 54b:15">B. Kam. 54ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>מה הפרט מפ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="Q01767"><he>פְּרָט</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 94b:6">B. Mets. 94ᵇ</cite> <he>שלישית בשואל מפ׳</he> that the third paragraph treats of a borrower, is explicitly stated (<cite ref="Exodus 22:13">Ex. XXII, 13</cite>).
<cite ref="Sotah 38a">Sot. 38ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>שם המפ׳</he> the special Name (the Tetragrammaton), v. supra.
<cite ref="Zevachim 53a">Zeb. 53ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="O01705"><he>סָתַם</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Chagigah 22b:6">Ḥag. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>ומה סתומות … מפ׳ וכ׳</he> if your undefined teachings are so well-founded, how much more your explicit teachings; a. fr.

Ned. 2ᵇ פתח … ומפרש ידות the Mishnah begins with kinnuyim …, and goes on explaining yadoth! Zeb. 13ᵃ ואין לי לפרש and I am unable to explain (the reason of the distinction between receiving and sprinkling the blood); אני אֲפָרֵשׁ I shall explain it.

<cite ref="Nedarim 81a:4-5">Ned. 81ᵃ</cite> <he>דבר זה … ולא פֵירְשׁוּהוּ עד שפֵּירְשׁוֹ וכ׳</he> that question (<cite ref="Jeremiah 9:11">Jer. IX, 11</cite>) was asked of prophets and scholars, and they could not explain it, until the Lord himself explained it (ib. 12).

<cite ref="Moed Katan 16b">M. Kat. 16ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Berakhot 18a:14">Ber. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>לא פֵירְשׁוּ לך</he> they did not interpret (the verse) to you; v. <cite ref="U01571"><he>שָׁנָה</he> I</cite>.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 31:8">Gen. R. s. 31</cite> <he>ולא פ׳</he> and did not explain (of what material the serpent was to be made); Y. R. Hash. III, end, 59ᵃ; a. fr.—Part. pass. as ab.
Meg. 3ᵃ, a. e. (ref. to Neh. VIII, 8) מפ׳ זה תרגום m’forash means interpretation.

senses.gloss: to be specified, defined; to be explained.
units: <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 6:6">Lev. R. s. 6</cite> <he>כל נביא שנתפ׳ וכ׳</he> a prophet whose name is stated. Gen. R. l. c. <he>בשלשה נ׳ ובאחד לא נ׳</he> in three places (in which <cite ref="P01466"><he>עֲשֵׂה</he></cite> occurs) the command is specified, but in the fourth (<cite ref="Numbers 21:8">Num. XXI, 8</cite>) it is not specified, v. supra.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 20:18">Yalk. Gen. 20</cite> <he>דבר שאינו מִתְפָּרֵשׁ בִמקימו וכ׳</he> a thing which is not defined in its original place but is defined in another passage; a. e.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 1:1">Yoma I, 1</cite> <he>מַפְרִישִׁין כהן וכ׳</he> they removed the high priest from his house to the cell &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Terumot 4:1">Ter. IV, 1</cite> <he>המַפְרִישׁ מקצת וכ׳</he> he who sets aside one portion of what is due of T’rumah or tithes.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 10:15">Num. R. s. 10</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Numbers 6:11">Num. VI, 11</cite>, <he>ועשה</he>) <he>שיַפְרִישֵׁם הכהן וכ׳</he> that the priest when offering them designates them, one for a sin-offering &c.

<cite ref="Numbers 6:11">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 23:32">Prov. XXIII, 32</cite>) <he>מה צפעון זה מפריש … כך היין מפריש וכ׳</he> as the adder divides between life and death, so wine removes from the ways of life to those of death; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 12:1">Lev. R. s. 12</cite> <he>כך ה׳ היין בין אדם וכ׳</he> so wine caused a separation between Adam and Eve; <he>ה׳ היין בין נח לבניו לעבדות</he> wine caused a division between Noah and his sons with regard to slavery; <he>ה׳ היין בין אהרן ובניו למיתה</he> wine caused a division between Aaron and his sons with regard to death; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 960">Yalk. Prov. 960</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Tamid 4:3">Tam. IV, 3</cite> <he>מן הכבד … ה׳</he> severed the lungs from the liver; a. fr.—Part. pass. <he>מוּפְרָשׁ</he>.
Ned. I, 1 מוּפְרְשַׁנִי ממך I will be separated from thee (will have no dealings with thee, accept no favors &c.); ib. 5ᵃ; a. e.—2) to go to sea.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 13">Gen. R. s. 13</cite> <he>היו מַפְרִישִׁין לים וכ׳</he> were crossing the ocean; a. e.
